title: IndexFile
description:
Top-level `.aristo/index.toml` document.

`__meta__` carries the schema version (currently `1`); every other key is an annotation id mapping to its [`IndexEntry`]. Iteration order follows `BTreeMap`'s sorted-by-key semantics so on-disk ordering is deterministic.

Note: serde forbids `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` together with `#[serde(flatten)]`, so unknown top-level keys flow into `entries` and either parse as `IndexEntry` (legal addition) or fail to parse against the entry schema (clear "unknown variant" / "missing field" error). Unknown-field rejection still happens INSIDE each entry via `IntentEntryWire` / `AssumeEntry`'s own `deny_unknown_fields`.

AnnotationId.description: Annotation id: local snake_case, stamp-assigned `aret_<alphanumeric>`, server-bound backed `aristos:<snake_case>`, or server-bound unbacked `kanon:<snake_case>`.

ArtaId.description: Opaque server identity, prefixed `arta_`, 8-64 alphanumeric chars.

CommitHash.description: Git commit hash: 40 lowercase hex chars (SHA-1) or 64 (SHA-256).

CoveredRegion.description: What syntactic region an annotation covers. Determines the body region hashed for staleness detection (per B3) and the scope a `"test"`-mode assertion is injected over.

oneOf.description: Whole function body (most common; α-form attribute on a fn).
A single statement (β-form macro before a stmt or loop).
The inline body of a module item.
A struct field or enum variant.

IndexEntry.description: One annotation's record in `.aristo/index.toml`. Tagged on `kind`: `kind = "intent"` deserializes as [`IntentEntry`]; `kind = "assume"` as [`AssumeEntry`].

oneOf.description: `assume` annotation: states an external invariant the code relies on. No `verify` (assumptions aren't verification targets per A5) and no `verified_outcome` (nothing is being verified). MAY be server-bound: the server can match an assumption against a known external-invariant template (per A5 + B5a), recorded as `linked`.

linked.description: Server-template binding (per A5 + B5a). No certificate companion because nothing is verified — that's why this stays a single `Option` rather than a [`BindingState`]-style enum.

Meta.description: `[__meta__]` header carrying the schema version plus optional generator metadata (who/when/where wrote the file; useful for debugging stale indices but not load-bearing for any logic).

generated_at.description: Timestamp of last write, RFC 3339 format (e.g., `"2026-05-13T14:23:00Z"`). Optional; informational only. String-typed (not a `DateTime`) to avoid pulling chrono / toml::Datetime into the public API; consumers can parse if needed.

generated_by.description: Identity of the writer (e.g., `"aristo index v0.1.0"`). Optional; informational only.

schema_version.description: Schema version of this index file. Always `1` in the current SDK.

source_root.description: Path to the source root the index was generated from, relative to the project root (e.g., `"."`). Optional; informational only.

ParentLink.description: Parent linkage: a single id or a list of ids (AND-semantics per C1/C2).

Status.description: Current verification state. The wire form uses kebab-case to keep `pending-deepen` readable on disk.

oneOf.description: Verified at the strongest method available; signature is current.
Verified via assertion-style testing (mined assertions, free or paid).
Was verified at a prior code state; current `body_hash` differs from the signed outcome. Sig still valid; only the code drifted.
`verified_outcome.commit_hash` is not in this repository's history. Most likely cause: index entry copied from another repo (B5b).
`verified_outcome` does not verify against any bundled public key — either tampered or signed by a revoked/unknown key (B5b).
Has not yet been verified, or was reverted to unknown after a rename or rebind operation invalidated the prior signature.
Sig is valid but commit ancestry could not be confirmed because the outcome's commit falls outside a shallow checkout's window (B5b).

Verification produced a counterexample — the property does NOT hold under the cited code/text version. Terminal state: stays Counterexample until either `body_hash` drifts (→ Stale) or the intent text is rewritten to exclude the refuted case. There is NO accept-counterexample flow; counterexamples are loud and surface on every `aristo stamp` until the user fixes them.

Verification was inconclusive — the verifier could not discharge the proof's gap and queued one or more suggested annotations the user could add to close it. Distinct from Unknown (which means "never attempted") so the skip logic can tell "we tried and got stuck" from "we haven't tried yet." Stays Inconclusive until either the source drifts (→ Stale via the body-drift rule), the user adopts a queued suggestion (→ re-verify), or the user explicitly re-runs with `--rerun`.

VerifyLevel.description:
`verify` field value. Mixed-type per design (G1):

- `false` (TOML bool): documentation only; no check ever runs. - `true` (TOML bool): resolves to project default in `aristo.toml [verify] default_method`. - one of `"neural"`, `"test"`, `"full"` (TOML string): named method.

VerifyMethod.description: Named verification methods (the string form of [`VerifyLevel`]).
